chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her; she may marry immediately if she wishes, and this counts as one irrevocable divorce. And if he had fixed a dowry (mahr) for her, she is entitled to half of what he fixed.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a wife divorced before consummation regarding her waiting period and dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of khulu' or talaq before dakhul, establishing that the woman is free to remarry immediately without an 'iddah (waiting period) since the marital bond was not fully consummated. It further specifies that the divorce counts as one of the three permissible divorces and entitles her to half the specified mahr, a ruling derived directly from the Quranic precedent. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for confirming the simplicity of the procedure and the proportional distribution of financial rights in pre-consummation divorces.
